articles.author: AR/VR News
articles.description:
Meta’s research arm is gearing up to wow SIGGRAPH 2025 with some wild mixed-reality prototypes. The “Tiramisu” headset cranks up realism with roughly 3× the contrast, 3.6× the angular resolution (90 PPD) and 14× the brightness (1,400 nits) of a Quest 3—trading off size, weight and a narrower FOV for visuals that might just pass a “visual Turing test.”  
On the flip side, the Boba 3 and Boba 3 VR models chase human-eye immersion with an enormous 180°×120° field of view and 4K×4K per-eye displays (up from 3K×3K in Boba 2). While these are purely lab demos that may never hit stores, they offer a thrilling glimpse at the next era of ultra-wide, hyper-real VR.
articles.title: Meta's prototype headsets show off the future of mixed reality

articles.author: AI News
articles.description:
OpenAI is beefing up ChatGPT’s mental-health guardrails by training it to better spot signs of emotional distress and share evidence-based resources when users might be struggling. The move, which involves experts and advisory groups, comes after reports that earlier versions sometimes fueled people’s delusions—and after the company rolled back an “overly sycophantic” update in April that made the chatbot too agreeable in harmful situations.
On top of that, ChatGPT will now prompt long-session users to “take a break” and, in “high-stakes” personal dilemmas (think “Should I break up with my partner?”), it’ll shy away from definitive answers, instead walking you through your options. These tweaks land just as OpenAI readies its GPT-5 model for release.
articles.title: ChatGPT will ‘better detect' mental distress after reports of it feeding people's delusions

articles.author: AI News
articles.description:
Truth Social’s new AI-fueled search, Truth Search AI, is basically a Fox News feeder: built on Perplexity’s tech and rolling out on the web (with apps soon), every test query points back to conservative sites—think Fox News, Fox Business, Washington Times and The Federalist—despite the platform’s big free-speech hustle.
Sure, it’ll spit out a grudgingly honest take (“Trump’s tariffs have stunted growth”), but the sourcing pool is so narrow it’s basically Trump Media’s Patriot Economy pump. CEO Devin Nunes calls it a “vital” beta and vows upgrades, while outside testers (hi, 404 Media) find glaring blind spots—like brushing off Trump’s ties in the Epstein files. Perplexity’s team? They’re just thrilled to serve “transparent citations,” even if they’re all red-state flavored.
articles.title: Truth Social's new AI search engine basically just pushes Fox News

articles.author: AI News
articles.description:
OpenAI has rolled out GPT-5 to free ChatGPT users and subscribers, touting it as “generally intelligent” — a step toward AGI, but not quite there. According to Sam Altman, it’s smarter, faster, and more accurate than GPT-4, with far fewer hallucinations. There are new model flavors (5, mini, nano in the API, plus Pro and Thinking in the $200/month tier) and pricing ranges from $0.05 to $10 per million tokens depending on variant and usage level.
Aside from raw speed, GPT-5 packs a 256k-token context window, Google app integrations (Gmail, Calendar, Contacts), and chat personalities like Cynic and Nerd. Early tests show big gains in coding and healthcare benchmarks, plus a significant drop in factual errors. With over 700 million people now using ChatGPT weekly, this upgrade should be hard to miss.
articles.title: OpenAI's GPT-5 Is Here

articles.author: Werliton Silva
articles.description:
So here's what happened...
I forked a project on GitHub because I wanted to contribute to one of its features.

But when I opened my fork - boom 💥 - only the main branch was there. All the other branches from the original repo? Gone.
At first, I thought something went wrong with the fork. But nope - that’s just how GitHub works.
When you fork a repo on GitHub, it only brings the default branch (usually main or master).

It does not copy over the other branches.
If the original repo had branches like:
feature/login
bugfix/style
refactor/api
You won’t see them in your fork.

But don't worry - they’re still there, just not in your copy… yet.
Here’s how I pulled the missing branches into my fork:
git remote add upstream https://github.com/original-user/original-repo.git

Replace that URL with the actual repo you forked from.
git fetch upstream

Now I could see all the remote branches by running:
git branch -r

I saw branches like:
upstream/feature/login
upstream/bugfix/style

Let’s say I needed the feature/login branch:
git checkout -b feature/login upstream/feature/login

Boom - now I had that branch locally.
If I wanted to work on it and push it to my forked repo:
git push origin feature/login

Now it exists on my GitHub too.

So if you ever fork a repo and wonder,  
"Where are the other branches?"  
They’re not missing - you just need to fetch them manually.
Hope this helps someone out there! ✌️
#git #github #devto #webdev #beginners
articles.title: I Forked a Repo but Only Got the `main` Branch - Here's What I Did
